name: Synthetic market signals working session
source: Synthetic fixture; no customer or confidential source material

facts.text: Market Signals is a synthetic support tool for reviewing public product conversations. It is not a sales forecast or a final decision.
A signal combines a customer situation, a need, buying factors, and links to public source posts.
The synthetic pipeline starts with about 12.4 million public posts and retains about 2.1 million after removing about 83 percent as ads, duplicates, organization-owned posts, or off-topic content.
The system reads each post in context, extracts a situation and need when present, and merges similar meanings into one signal.
Each signal links to the public source posts used as evidence.
Signals are classified as evergreen, trending, or event-driven based on how they change over time.
The synthetic dashboard has Signals, Market Comparison, and Customer Situations screens.
The proposed review examines 5–10 signals and collects short comments about realism, usefulness, product fit, use, and scope.
The next phase asks which decisions, public sources, comparison groups, and review frequency would be most useful.

unknowns.text: The synthetic material does not state precision, recall, accuracy, confidence thresholds, or a classification guarantee.
The synthetic material does not specify consent, retention, licenses, legal review, or privacy controls.
The synthetic material does not claim revenue lift, conversion improvement, forecast accuracy, or campaign ROI.
The synthetic material does not provide a committed launch date, production SLA, owner, or approved rollout scope.
The 12.4 million, 2.1 million, and 83 percent figures are synthetic examples, not audited current measurements.
The synthetic material does not name a model, training data, embedding method, clustering algorithm, or threshold.

scenarios.title: Executive asks what the synthetic dashboard changes

script.speaker: presenter
script.text: This is a synthetic dashboard for public product conversations.

script.speaker: customer
script.text: What decision can this dashboard improve, and is it a sales forecast?

answerHints: Position it as one review input.
State that it is not a forecast or ROI claim.

scenarios.title: Reviewer challenges the synthetic filtering example

script.speaker: customer
script.text: You went from 12.4 million posts to 2.1 million. Why should I trust an 83% removal rate?

scenarios.title: Engineer asks how signals are produced

script.speaker: customer
script.text: How does the system create signals, and which clustering model and threshold do you use?

answerHints: Say model details are not specified.

scenarios.title: Product lead asks how to use signal types

script.speaker: customer
script.text: How would evergreen, trending, and event-driven signals change product and content work?

answerHints: Connect types to different review cadences.

scenarios.title: Privacy reviewer challenges traceability and controls

script.speaker: customer
script.text: Can I inspect the evidence, and are privacy, consent, and retention requirements covered?

answerHints: State that privacy controls are not specified.

scenarios.title: Sponsor asks for a rollout plan

script.speaker: customer
script.text: What should we do after this session, how often should we review it, and can you launch next month?

answerHints: Review 5–10 signals and agree a cadence.
Do not accept a launch date.

scenarios.title: Question not answered by the synthetic material

script.speaker: customer
script.text: What are the measured precision and recall for extraction by source?

answerHints: Say the measurements are not provided.
Offer validation before relying on them.

scenarios.title: User asks where to start

script.speaker: customer
script.text: Which screen should a regular review start with, and can we drill into the source?

answerHints: Suggest a screen order as a proposal.
Confirm that public source posts are inspectable.
